title: Phishing leads to email account takeover
description: A member of staff types their Microsoft 365 password into a fake login page. MFA is not switched on, so the attacker can log in from anywhere, read years of client email and send emails as the practice.
recommended_control: Turn on MFA for every Microsoft 365 account. Block automatic forwarding of email to outside addresses. Short phishing awareness session for all staff, repeated every year.
ten_steps: Identity and access management; Engagement and training
est_cost: £0 plus about 1 hour of staff time

title: Payment and bank detail fraud
description: A criminal using a hijacked or look-alike email address tells a client, or the practice, to pay money into a new bank account. Staff currently act on emailed bank detail changes without checking.
recommended_control: Written rule: any new or changed bank details are confirmed by phone, using a number already on file, before any payment. Mark emails from outside the practice with an [EXTERNAL] tag. MFA from R01 removes the easiest route in.

title: Ransomware through unpatched software
description: Updates are installed when staff get round to it. Several laptops are weeks behind on Windows and browser updates, and old copies of Java and a PDF reader are installed but not used.
existing_controls: Microsoft Defender Antivirus is on by default on the Windows 11 laptops
recommended_control: Turn on automatic updates for every device and app and check them weekly. Install critical and high-risk updates within 14 days, as Cyber Essentials requires. Remove software nobody uses.

title: Backups would not survive ransomware
description: The shared drive on the NAS is copied every night to a USB disk that is always plugged in, so ransomware could encrypt both. Nobody has ever tested a restore. Email and OneDrive files are not backed up separately.
existing_controls: Nightly copy to an always-connected USB disk
recommended_control: Keep at least one backup copy offline or in cloud storage that cannot be changed or deleted. Add a backup service for Microsoft 365. Test restoring files every quarter and write down the result.

title: Reused and weak passwords
description: Staff choose their own passwords and several reuse personal ones. There is no password manager. Passwords are kept in a notebook at reception and in a spreadsheet on the shared drive.
recommended_control: Give every member of staff a business password manager. Delete the password spreadsheet and shred the notebook. Use three random words for the few passwords people must remember. Turn on MFA wherever a service offers it.

title: Everyone is an administrator
description: All staff log in to their laptops with full administrator rights. The practice manager's everyday Microsoft 365 account is also a global admin. Any malware a user opens runs with those same rights.
recommended_control: Remove admin rights from everyday accounts. Create separate admin accounts, with MFA, used only for admin tasks. The IT contractor installs software on request.

title: Former staff accounts still active
description: Two people left in the last year. One of their Microsoft 365 accounts is still enabled and licensed. The shared login to the accounting software has not been changed since either of them left.
existing_controls: Leavers are removed from the payroll only
recommended_control: Use a leavers checklist on each person's last day: disable their accounts, remove them from every cloud service, change any shared passwords and collect devices. Check the account list against the staff list every quarter. Replace shared logins with named ones.

title: Lost or stolen laptop without encryption
description: Seven of the ten laptops have no disk encryption. Staff carry them between home, the office and client sites. A stolen laptop would expose every client file synced to it.
recommended_control: Turn on BitLocker on every laptop and store the recovery keys in Microsoft 365. Lock screens after a few minutes idle and lock the device after no more than 10 wrong attempts.

title: Unsupported Windows 10 PC at reception
description: The reception PC runs Windows 10, which Microsoft stopped supporting on 14 October 2025. No Extended Security Updates were bought. It is used for email, web browsing and scanning client ID documents.
recommended_control: Replace it with a Windows 11 PC, or upgrade it if the hardware allows. Until then, stop using it for email and web browsing.

title: Home working on a shared family PC
description: The part-time bookkeeper works from a family PC at home that the whole household uses with one shared login. Other staff sometimes work from cafe and train Wi-Fi.
recommended_control: Give the bookkeeper a company laptop. Keep the Windows firewall on for every network. Give staff a one-page home and travel working guide.

title: Compromise of a key supplier
description: The practice depends on its cloud accounting and practice software, its payroll software and a pay-as-you-go IT contractor. The contractor uses a shared admin@ account whose password three people know. A breach at any supplier could expose client data or stop work.
recommended_control: List each supplier and the data it holds. Check each has Cyber Essentials or similar and supports MFA. Give the IT contractor a named admin account with MFA. Export key client data from the accounting software every month.

title: Office router and NAS exposed to the internet
description: Remote administration is switched on for the office router and its admin password has never been changed. A previous IT contractor opened a port so staff could reach the NAS from home, which puts its login page on the internet with no MFA. Its firmware is a year out of date.
existing_controls: The router blocks other inbound connections by default
recommended_control: Change the router admin password and turn off remote admin. Close the NAS port and use OneDrive or SharePoint for remote file access instead. Write down each inbound rule and the business reason for it. Update the NAS firmware.

title: Personal phones with work email
description: About ten staff read work email on their own phones. There is no rule requiring a screen lock, and some phones are too old to get updates.
recommended_control: Only allow work email on phones with a screen lock and a supported operating system, using app protection policies in Microsoft 365. Be able to wipe work data from a lost phone.
est_cost: Included in the Microsoft 365 Business Premium upgrade

title: No plan for handling a cyber incident
description: Nobody knows who makes decisions in an incident, how to reach the IT contractor out of hours, or that a serious personal data breach must be reported to the ICO within 72 hours.
recommended_control: Write a one-page incident plan: who decides, who to call, ICO reporting, Action Fraud, the insurer and a template message to clients. Practise it once a year using the NCSC's free Exercise in a Box.

title: Client data sent the wrong way
description: Staff email tax returns and ID scans as attachments, sometimes to the wrong address through autocomplete. Occasionally files are sent from personal email or WhatsApp when Microsoft 365 is slow.
recommended_control: Send documents to clients through the client portal, not email attachments. Ban personal email and messaging apps for client data. Add a short delay to outgoing email so mistakes can be stopped.
